messages:
maya: Hey team — heads-up: we need to finalize the telemetry contract between runtime + infra for the new metrics we plan to surface in Console. Goal is to have dashboards + alerting wired before the rollout next sprint. :wave:

simon: Quick q — which metrics are must-haves vs nice-to-have? I can push runtime PRs but need exact metric names, tag schema, and expected cardinality.

maya: Must-haves: 1) inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 (by model, region, instance_type), 2) request.error_rate (by route + model), 3) kv_cache.hit_rate (model, route), 4) serving.qps (per pool). Nice-to-have: batch_size_dist, inferred_seq_len_histogram.

prateek: From infra side we need consistent labels: team=, env=, model_version=, pool_id=. Also a stable metric prefix: `redwood.serving.*`. Can runtime add `pool_id` on each request so we can filter by Dedicated vs Hosted?

simon: Yes — runtime can add `pool_id` tag. We'll name metrics exactly as Maya listed and emit `redwood.serving.inference_latency_ms` (histogram) and `redwood.serving.request_errors_total` (counter).

lee: For oncall routing and alerting: we want alerts split into two planes — infra-capacity (routes to infra oncall) vs product-UX regressions (routes to runtime/product). Example: high burn rate of SLO should go to runtime/product; host-level OOMs go to infra. We also need a paging policy that avoids noise during deploy windows.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: alerts include `escalation_key` label so the Alertmanager mapping can route to the right rotation. We'll keep a small mapping table in the Console config. Also plan a deploy-silence window flag developers can set when doing controlled rollouts.

lee: Draft alert example (please review thresholds — we can iterate after we have baseline stats):
```yaml
alert: InferenceLatencyP95High
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_serving_inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region)) > 0.6
labels:
  severity: page
  escalation: runtime-oncall
annotations:
  summary: "P95 latency for model {{ $labels.model }} in {{ $labels.region }} > 600ms"
```

prateek: On infra side we'll add a derived metric `redwood.serving.slo_burn_rate` that computes 5m burn rate from the SLO evaluation job. We can then have an alert rule: if burn_rate > 1.2 for 10m -> page runtime/product.

simon: Two implementation notes: 1) runtime will expose histograms in seconds (rename to `_seconds`), but Console expects ms for the UI — we can convert in the dashboard queries. 2) We'll add label `deployment_stage` (can be `canary`, `stable`) so alerts during canary can be routed to the release owner first.

maya: Good. Action items: 
- simon: open PR with metric names + example exports + tag list (due EOD tomorrow).
- prateek: add `slo_burn_rate` derived metric and Alertmanager routing keys (due in 3 working days).
- lee: propose paging thresholds and silence policy for deploy windows (due in 2 days).
- maya: prototype Console dashboard with the canonical queries and the routing mapping (I'll do initial mock).

infra-ci-bot: New doc uploaded: https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry/contracts/serving-metrics-v1 (permissions: eng-platform, eng-runtime, infra).

maya: I'll sync up with Legal for any telemetry PII checks but these metrics are all system-level. If anyone has objections to labels or metric names shout now. :eyes:

simon: LGTM. I'll start the PR and tag runtime owners.

lee: One more ask — add an `alert_origin` label so our incident automation can include the relevant runbook link automatically.

prateek: Will do. Also will add `team` label so we can aggregate cross-team totals.

maya: Thanks all — I'll create a short rollout checklist once PRs land and we have baseline numbers to pick thresholds. :thumbsup:
